prompt.en: You called CQ at 15 words per minute even though you copy new calls at 9, and the answering station comes back too fast. What combined response is best?

text.en: Ask for slower sending now, then make future CQs at a speed you can receive accurately.
Keep sending at 15 because a clean keyer setting proves the reply will be copyable.
Change frequency without explanation, because QSY is the normal request for slower code.
Send a higher RST strength report so the other station knows to slow down.

explanation.en: QRS handles the immediate too-fast reply, and the CQ speed rule prevents causing the same problem in the next call.

prompt.en: Before calling CQ on CW, you send QRL? and hear static crashes plus a weak station fragment. Which decision best combines the Q-signal rules?

text.en: Recognize the static as QRN, but do not call CQ until you are satisfied the frequency is not in use.
Treat QRN as permission to transmit because static means no station can be using the frequency.
Send QRZ? because any weak fragment before your CQ must be someone calling you.
Send QSY as the first call, because changing frequency is the same as checking whether one is busy.

explanation.en: QRN describes static trouble, while QRL? is the busy-frequency check. Noise does not cancel the need to protect a frequency that may already be occupied.

prompt.en: A Morse test signal drops one S-unit after the receiving station changes antennas, and the note also becomes rough. Which report reasoning is best?

text.en: Do not infer a transmitter-power change from the S-meter, but do reflect the rough note in the tone part of RST.
Calculate one-quarter transmitter power and keep tone perfect because S-meter readings decide all RST digits.
Remove the tone digit because any antenna change turns a Morse report into a voice report.
Raise the readability digit automatically because a lower S-meter proves the signal is easier to understand.

explanation.en: The S-unit power shortcut requires unchanged conditions, and RST has separate observations. A changed antenna breaks the power inference; a rough Morse note belongs in tone quality.
